title: Service Discovery with Netflix Eureka
description: Use Eureka to dynamically locate services without hard‑coding URLs.

slides.title: Why Service Discovery? 🧭
slides.content:
# The Problem

In a microservices environment, instances come and go (auto‑scaling, failures). Hard‑coding IP addresses or hostnames is impossible.

**Solution:** Service registry (like Netflix Eureka). Services register themselves, and clients look up the registry to find other services.

quizData.question: What is the role of a service registry in microservices?

options.text: To keep track of available service instances

quizData.explanation: A service registry (like Eureka) stores the network locations of available service instances so clients can discover them dynamically.

slides.title: Setting Up a Eureka Server
Registering a Service with Eureka
slides.content:
Add `spring-cloud-starter-netflix-eureka-client` to your microservice. Then in `application.properties`:

```properties
spring.application.name=user-service
eureka.client.serviceUrl.defaultZone=http://localhost:8761/eureka/
```

Now your service registers with Eureka. The `@FeignClient(name="user-service")` will use the registry to find instances.

slides.title: Eureka Heartbeats
slides.content: Services send heartbeats to Eureka every 30 seconds. If a service fails to send three consecutive heartbeats, it's removed from the registry – preventing calls to dead instances.
